also: I’ll be darned if I ever

terms.gloss: may the gods destroy me if …
evidence: Plaut. Mil. 3.2.21: Dī mē perdant, sī bibī (Lewis & Short s.v. enim)
terms.comment: An oath on oneself: what follows sī is what the speaker denies.

evidence: Cic. Att. 13.25.3: male mī sit, sī umquam quicquam tam ēnītar
terms.comment: “May it go badly with me if …”, with the future after sī: Cicero swears to Atticus that he will never again take such pains over a piece of writing.
terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Cic. in epistulīs

phrases.latin: Dī mē perdant, sī ego tuī quicquam abstulī.
phrases.english: May the gods destroy me if I took anything of yours.
I’ll be damned if I know.
I’ll be darned if I ever …

phrases.latin: Male mī sit, sī umquam quicquam tam ēnītar.
phrases.english: I’ll be damned if I ever take such pains over anything again.
